newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui aid to builder boosts construction shares
newsitem.headline: Mitsui aid to builder boosts construction shares

text.p: Giant industrial group Mitsui said on Wednesday it would give full backing to debt-ridden member firm Mitsui Construction Co, news that helped brighten sentiment towards Japan's troubled construction sector.

The backing was pledged after Mitsui Construction, which like the whole sector is suffering the after-effects of the collapse of Japan's late-1980s asset price bubble, presented group firms with a three-year restructuring programme.

Four financial institutions in the group -- Sakura Bank Ltd, Mitsui Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Mitsui Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd and Mitsui Mutual Life Insurance Co -- would all provide financial support, a spokesman for Mitsui Marine said.
Details of the financial support, however, had yet to be decided, he said.

Stock market investors, troubled by the failure of two large builders last month and worried that more could follow, welcomed the news with purchases of shares throughout the construction sector, making it the bourse's second-best performing sector for the session.
The buying also helped Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index recoup most of the losses it suffered earlier on Wednesday. It closed down 0.47 percent at 19,008.60.

The bourse suspended trading in Mitsui Construction shares late in the afternoon, in order to give the market time to get clarification of the restructuring plan. Prior to the suspension the shares were trading at 170 yen, up 11 yen from Tuesday's close.
"The Mitsui Construction news was a relief to the market and helped make sentiment somewhat brighter," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.

Mitsui Construction said that, under its restructuring scheme, it will cut its workforce by 400 over the next three years from 4,400 employees as of March. It also said it will slim down unprofitable operations and sell off assets owned by the company and its affiliates.
It aims to cut its liabilities, including debts and guarantees of affiliates' debts, by 74 billion yen ($637 million) by 1999, from 493 billion yen ($4.25 billion) as of March 31 this year.
By taking such steps, it hopes to post a parent current profit of 10 billion yen ($86.2 million) in the year to March 31, 2000, against a 2.67 billion yen ($23.0 million) profit in 1996/97.
"We will support (the) restructuring plan Mitsui Construction submitted, while cooperating and coordinating with other members in the Mitsui group," a Sakura Bank spokesman said.

A spokesman for Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd, Mitsui Construction's largest shareholder with a 15.6 percent stake, said his firm would cooperate with the builder by placing orders with it and helping it sell off assets.
He added, however, that Mitsui Fudosan would not risk its own profits in the process.
Susumu Naito, a managing director at Mitsui Construction, told a news conference that his company would also ask for support from financial institutions outside the Mitsui group.
He said it may ask financial institutions to accept a third-party allocation of new shares to increase its capital and to lower interest rate payments on its debts.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said in its Wednesday evening edition that Mitsui Construction was unlikely to face fund shortages in the near future but was struggling with huge debts and meagre profits.
